webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey test asserts only the UI error after failed re-auth password attempts and does not verify the LOGIN_ERROR/INVALID_USER_CREDENTIALS event before events.clear(), unlike the older passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey test

Method `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel)` has misleading name/inverted semantics: returns false when user is null, meaning 'passkeys enabled and user already identified' rather than just 'passkeys enabled'; should move null check to call sites or rename, and shares a confusing same name with no-arg `UsernameForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()`

Cross-package dependency leak: `authenticators.util.AuthenticatorUtils` imports a constant from `authenticators.browser.AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator`, forcing the constant to be widened from protected to public; the shared state key should live in a shared location or the helper should stay in the browser package

Likely duplicated/now-dead re-auth check: `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormFormError` re-implements the auth-note read of `isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth`, creating either dead code or two drifting implementations; the util method should delegate to or replace the existing helper

~55-line test method `webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication` duplicated verbatim across two test classes (PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest and PasskeysUsernameFormTest), risking divergent copies; should be extracted to a shared test base/utility

Anti-pattern assert-then-fail-in-catch in `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` test: swallows any exception (including driver failures), so a broken test could falsely pass; should use `driver.findElements` and assert empty, or `Assert.assertThrows`; pattern repeated twice in the same method

Behavioral asymmetry in `UsernamePasswordForm`: `fillContextForm` no longer called when user is null, changing conditional-UI setup on the initial login form, but the comments still describe the old semantics and the responsibility shift is undocumented, risking a regression of conditional UI on the initial login page
WebAuthn conditional UI re-authentication uses an empty allowList, allowing a different user's passkey to complete re-auth (prompt=login) and potentially swapping identity mid-session
UsernameForm.authenticate skip condition regression: realm-level passkey policy forces re-auth users without passkeys back to the username form; the UsernameForm path is untested

UsernameForm calls no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() which is not defined in this diff; UsernameForm does not extend UsernamePasswordForm, so code may not compile (or has confusing duplicate logic)

UsernamePasswordForm.challenge/authenticate no longer fills WebAuthn form data on the initial (user==null) login page, potentially breaking initial passkey login rendering for flows built only around UsernamePasswordForm
USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH visibility changed from protected to public, unnecessarily broadening the SPI API surface

Fragile 'assert element absent' test pattern in reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey swallows generic Exceptions, letting unexpected errors like StaleElementReferenceException silently pass; should use assertThrows instead

adjudication_records.issue_text: Misleading guard name: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled reads as a pure feature check but silently requires user != null, which will return false during first-factor authentication for future callers using it as a realm-feature probe

adjudication.rationale: In UsernamePasswordForm a new helper `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` was added that returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. The name reads like a pure "feature enabled" predicate, but it also encodes a runtime state condition (`user != null`). That can be misleading for reuse: a caller might reasonably use it to check whether passkeys/conditional UI are enabled at the realm/feature level, but it will return false whenever no user is selected (e.g., initial first-factor screen). This is a diff-grounded API/clarity concern rather than a verifiable functional defect in the current call sites, which intentionally pass `context.getUser()`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: UsernameForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() checks only realm policy, not whether the re-authenticating user actually has a passkey credential, forcing an extra username interaction for users without WebAuthn credentials during re-auth

adjudication.rationale: In `UsernameForm.authenticate`, the fast-path that skips the username screen during re-auth (`context.getUser() != null`) is now disabled whenever `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` returns true (`if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()) { ... context.success(); }`). The finding’s core concern is that this gate appears to be based on passkeys being enabled in general (method name suggests realm-level feature/policy) rather than on whether the already-identified re-authenticating user actually has a WebAuthn/passkey credential, which could cause an unnecessary extra username step for users without passkeys when the realm has passkeys enabled. The diff does not show `UsernameForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` implementation, so the “checks only realm policy” part can’t be fully verified here, but the introduced dependency on this method for re-auth skipping is diff-grounded and creates a concrete UX/flow edge-case concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing test coverage for the case of passkeys enabled for realm but user has no passkey credential during re-authentication

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds multiple re-authentication tests for users with passkeys (e.g., `webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication`, `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthentication`) and a test for re-authentication when realm passkeys are disabled (`reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` sets `setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)`). However, there is no test covering the specific scenario where passkeys are enabled for the realm (`isPasskeysEnabled()` true) but the re-authenticating user has no WebAuthn/passkey credential; given the new behavior to fill/show conditional passkey UI during re-auth when `user != null` (`UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user)` and `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm`), this is a concrete missing test for newly adjusted logic rather than a proven functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: UsernameForm.authenticate() calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() without arguments while UsernamePasswordForm requires a UserModel, potentially causing a compile error or a UX regression where password-only users in passkeys-enabled realms see the username form during re-auth

adjudication_records.issue_text: Conditional-UI setup (fillContextForm) is no longer invoked on the initial user-unknown login page because the new gate requires user != null, breaking first-visit discoverable-passkey autofill on the combined username/password page

adjudication.rationale: In `UsernamePasswordForm`, `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` used to run when passkeys were enabled even if `context.getUser()` was null (and in `challenge(...)` it explicitly ran only when user was null). The change introduces `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` which additionally requires `user != null`, and both call sites now gate on that (`authenticate(...)` and `challenge(...)`). Therefore, on the initial combined username/password page where the user is typically not yet identified (`context.getUser() == null`), `fillContextForm` will no longer be invoked, a concrete behavioral change that can break passkey/conditional-UI setup on first visit.

adjudication_records.issue_text: WebAuthnAuthenticator.shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators() only checks user != null without verifying the user owns webauthn credentials, potentially rendering a passkey prompt for users with no passkeys

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not introduce behavior that would render WebAuthn authenticators for users without WebAuthn credentials. `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm()` previously gated on `user != null`; the new `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context)` defaults to the same check (`return context.getUser() != null;`). Additionally, `fillContextForm()` still builds a `WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean` and checks `authenticators.getAuthenticators().isEmpty()` (logic beyond that line is unchanged in the diff), which is the mechanism that would prevent showing authenticators when the user has none. The finding misattributes missing credential ownership verification to the new method; nothing in the diff removes/changes the existing empty-authenticators handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-generic error message during re-authentication leaks username validity by showing 'Invalid password.' instead of a generic invalid credentials message

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not change error-message selection logic (e.g., switching from a generic invalid-credentials message to "Invalid password."); it only refactors re-authentication form setup into `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context)` and adjusts when passkeys UI is shown. The added/updated tests assert "Invalid password." during re-authentication flows, but the diff provides no evidence that this behavior newly leaks username validity (reauthentication implies `context.getUser()` is already set and username is already known/hidden).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Repeated credential materialization on every failed password attempt: new isConditionalPasskeysEnabled gate in UsernamePasswordForm.challenge causes fillContextForm to run on every error re-challenge, triggering a credential-store query and WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean construction on the error path; consider caching the bean in the auth session note or short-circuiting before building it when only an error re-render is needed

adjudication.rationale: While the diff does make UsernamePasswordForm call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on error re-challenges when isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) is true, the finding’s specific claim that this “triggers a credential-store query and WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean construction” is not supported by the diff. WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm() was changed to only construct WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean when shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context) is true, and WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator overrides shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators() to return false (so no bean construction/credential lookup in that path). Thus the stated expensive repeated materialization is a misread of the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: fillContextForm is invoked twice on the error path in WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse, though it is cheap (form attribute setup only) since shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators returns false

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse(...)` contains exactly one explicit call to `fillContextForm(context)` before returning `errorChallenge.apply(context)`. The finding claims `fillContextForm` is invoked twice on the error path, but the diff does not show `errorChallenge.apply(context)` calling `fillContextForm` (or otherwise causing a second invocation). While `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(...)` is overridden to return `false`, that doesn’t demonstrate a double invocation either—only that `fillContextForm` would skip listing authenticators when called.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Conditional-UI WebAuthn setup logic inverted: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user) requires user != null, so the initial login page (user not yet identified) no longer fills the WebAuthn context form, breaking passkey autofill on UsernamePasswordForm's first-factor page

adjudication.rationale: In `UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate()` the call to `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` was previously executed in the path where the user was not yet selected (comment: “when the user is not already selected” and no `user != null` check). The diff moves this to an unconditional block guarded by `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, and `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` now explicitly requires `user != null`. The same guard is used in `challenge(context, error, field)`. This means when `context.getUser()` is null on the initial first-factor username/password screen, WebAuthn conditional UI context will no longer be filled by this form, which can break passkey conditional UI/autofill setup on that initial page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing test coverage: no test asserts the webauthn form is present on the initial page with user == null (e.g. after entering a wrong username); tests only cover the user-selected and re-auth paths

adjudication.rationale: The diff *does* add/contain tests asserting the WebAuthn form is present before any user is selected (i.e., on the initial login page when `context.getUser()` would typically be null). For example, in `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.passwordLoginWithExternalKey()` and `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthentication()`, after `oauth.openLoginForm()` the tests assert `driver.findElement(By.xpath("//form[@id='webauth']"))` is not null. Therefore the claim that "no test asserts the webauthn form is present on the initial page with user == null" is contradicted by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: UsernameForm behavior change: re-authenticating users now always see a username prompt when passkeys are enabled at realm level, even users with no passkey credential, bypassing the previous seamless re-auth skip

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `UsernameForm.authenticate()` from `if (context.getUser() != null) { ... context.success(); }` to `if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()) { ... context.success(); }`, meaning re-authentication no longer skips the username step when conditional passkeys are enabled. From the diff we can verify this UX/flow change, but we cannot verify that `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` is purely “realm-level” (its implementation isn’t shown here) or that it accounts for whether the user actually has a passkey credential. If it doesn’t, this could unnecessarily force identified users without passkeys through an extra username prompt (a regression in seamless re-auth), but it’s not a correctness break proven by the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: UsernameForm.authenticate() calls undefined method isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() at UsernameForm.java:47 — method only exists in UsernamePasswordForm with a different signature, likely compile break

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `UsernameForm.authenticate()` now calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no args, but the diff does not show the full `UsernameForm` class (it may already define this method below the shown hunk or inherit it from a superclass). While `UsernamePasswordForm` adds a different `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel)` method, that doesn’t prove `UsernameForm` lacks a no-arg version. Therefore the claimed compile break (“undefined method”) is not verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: WebAuthn data no longer set on first-time login when user is not yet identified in UsernamePasswordForm.java:113 — fillContextForm never invoked when user is null, removing passkey login entry point on initial page

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that `UsernamePasswordForm` no longer calls `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` when `context.getUser()` is null: both in `authenticate()` and in the error `challenge()` path it now gates on `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, which requires `user != null`. Previously it filled WebAuthn context when passkeys were enabled even without a selected user. However, the finding’s claim that this definitively “remov[es] passkey login entry point on initial page” can’t be proven from this diff alone because the passkey UI might be set up by other authenticators/templates (e.g., `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator`) not shown here. So it’s a concrete, diff-grounded potential regression/behavior change to validate, but not a verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm returns null when user has no webauthn credentials, skipping all other form setup and silently losing webauthn attributes with no error or logging

adjudication.rationale: The diff only changes the condition guarding the existing logic from `if (user != null)` to `if (shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context))`, with the default implementation returning `context.getUser() != null`. The early `return null` when `authenticators.getAuthenticators().isEmpty()` remains unchanged and isn’t shown as newly introduced or altered here, nor does the diff demonstrate any “other form setup” that would be skipped or “webauthn attributes” being lost as a result of this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey catches generic Exception instead of NoSuchElementException, masking real Selenium/driver failures

adjudication.rationale: In `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey`, the diff adds two blocks that do `driver.findElement(By.xpath("//form[@id='webauth']"))` inside a `try` and then `catch (Exception nsee) { // expected }`. This is broader than necessary (it should typically catch `NoSuchElementException` for the "element not present" case) and could indeed mask unrelated Selenium/driver/runtime failures, weakening the test’s ability to detect real issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Broken negative assertion in PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey: the try/catch pattern with assertThat nullValue and catch(Exception) swallows AssertionErrors and makes fail() unreachable, so the test passes whether or not the WebAuthn button is rendered

adjudication.rationale: In PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey, the try/catch does not “swallow AssertionErrors”: it catches only Exception, while Hamcrest/JUnit assertion failures throw AssertionError (an Error), which would still fail the test if the WebAuthn form is present. When the element is absent, driver.findElement(...) throws (e.g., NoSuchElementException) before assertThat is evaluated, which is caught and treated as expected. So the test does not pass “whether or not the WebAuthn button is rendered,” though the pattern is awkward/redundant and makes fail() effectively unreachable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test covers the re-authentication error path in WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse, leaving the setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError call (USERNAME_HIDDEN/REGISTRATION_DISABLED setup) untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new logic in `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse` to call `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context)` (which sets `LoginFormsProvider.USERNAME_HIDDEN` and `REGISTRATION_DISABLED` when the `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` auth note is true). The added/modified tests exercise re-authentication via `prompt=login` and some password-failure scenarios, but none appear to trigger the *passkey failure* path that would invoke `createErrorResponse` (i.e., conditional WebAuthn error handling). There is also no assertion in tests around the username-hidden/registration-disabled form attributes, so this newly introduced behavior is not covered.

adjudication_records.issue_text: UsernameForm.authenticate behavioral change showing the username form during re-auth for users with linked IDP brokers when conditional passkeys are enabled is untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes UsernameForm.authenticate() to *not* skip the username form during re-authentication when conditional passkeys are enabled (`if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()) { ... }`). This bypasses the existing re-auth shortcut logic that conditionally calls `context.success()` only when there are no linked brokers (`!this.hasLinkedBrokers(context)`). The newly added/updated tests exercise passkeys + re-auth flows, but none cover the specific case of a re-authenticated user who has linked IDP brokers under conditional passkeys, so this behavioral change/edge case is not directly tested in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: UsernameForm.java:47 calls a no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() that may not exist — the only method in the diff is the (UserModel) overload in sibling class UsernamePasswordForm, potentially causing a compile error

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `UsernameForm.authenticate()` to call a no-arg `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` (`if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled())`). In the provided diff, no such no-arg method is added to `UsernameForm` (or shown in a shared superclass/util), while a similarly named method is only introduced in the sibling `UsernamePasswordForm` but with a different signature (`isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`). If `UsernameForm` (or its parents) does not already define the no-arg method, this change would introduce a compile error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey test asserts only the UI error after failed re-auth password attempts and does not verify the LOGIN_ERROR/INVALID_USER_CREDENTIALS event before events.clear(), unlike the older passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey test

adjudication.rationale: In `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest#webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey`, the test performs an intentional failed re-authentication password attempt (`loginPage.login(getPassword("test-user@localhost")); Assert.assertEquals("Invalid password.", loginPage.getInputError());`) and then calls `events.clear()` without asserting a corresponding `LOGIN_ERROR` event (e.g., `Errors.INVALID_USER_CREDENTIALS`). By contrast, `passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey` explicitly asserts `events.expect(EventType.LOGIN_ERROR)...error(Errors.INVALID_USER_CREDENTIALS)`. This is a concrete test coverage gap specific to the newly added scenario, not a product bug shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Method `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel)` has misleading name/inverted semantics: returns false when user is null, meaning 'passkeys enabled and user already identified' rather than just 'passkeys enabled'; should move null check to call sites or rename, and shares a confusing same name with no-arg `UsernameForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()`

adjudication.rationale: In `UsernamePasswordForm`, the newly added `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`, so it’s not purely “passkeys enabled” but “passkeys enabled AND a user is already identified”. The call sites were also changed to rely on this (`authenticate()` and `challenge()` now guard `fillContextForm` via this method), and the nearby comment says “setup webauthn data when passkeys enabled”, which no longer matches the actual condition. Additionally, `UsernameForm` already has a different `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` (no-arg) used in `if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled())`, making the shared name potentially confusing. This is a clarity/API naming issue rather than a demonstrable functional defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cross-package dependency leak: `authenticators.util.AuthenticatorUtils` imports a constant from `authenticators.browser.AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator`, forcing the constant to be widened from protected to public; the shared state key should live in a shared location or the helper should stay in the browser package

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `AuthenticatorUtils` (in `authenticators.util`) adding `import static org.keycloak.authentication.authenticators.browser.AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH;` and using it in `setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(...)`. To make that accessible, `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` is changed from `protected static final` to `public static final`. This is a verifiable cross-package coupling introduced by the change, and the finding’s suggested remediation (move the key to a shared location or keep helper in the browser package) is a concrete architectural concern rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Likely duplicated/now-dead re-auth check: `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormFormError` re-implements the auth-note read of `isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth`, creating either dead code or two drifting implementations; the util method should delegate to or replace the existing helper

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the prior inline re-authentication check in `badPasswordHandler` was removed and replaced by a single extracted utility method `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context)`. In the shown changes there is no duplicated logic co-existing (the old block is gone), and the finding references a non-existent method name (`...FormFormError`). Whether an `isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth` helper still exists/gets used elsewhere isn’t verifiable from this diff alone, so the claim of “two drifting implementations”/dead code is not grounded here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ~55-line test method `webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication` duplicated verbatim across two test classes (PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest and PasskeysUsernameFormTest), risking divergent copies; should be extracted to a shared test base/utility

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new test method `webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication` to both `PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest` and `PasskeysUsernameFormTest`, and the bodies are effectively the same sequence (configure passkeys policy for discoverable keys, register user, logout, auto-login via discoverable key, then re-auth with `prompt=login` and assert another passkey login event). This is a real, diff-grounded duplication/maintainability concern (risk of future divergence), not a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Anti-pattern assert-then-fail-in-catch in `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` test: swallows any exception (including driver failures), so a broken test could falsely pass; should use `driver.findElements` and assert empty, or `Assert.assertThrows`; pattern repeated twice in the same method

adjudication.rationale: In `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey`, the diff adds two blocks `try { driver.findElement(...); fail(...) } catch (Exception nsee) { // expected }`. This catches any `Exception`, not just `NoSuchElementException`, so unrelated WebDriver/test failures could be swallowed and the test could falsely pass. This is a real, diff-grounded test-quality issue (better to use `findElements().isEmpty()` or `assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)`), but it does not indicate a product/runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Behavioral asymmetry in `UsernamePasswordForm`: `fillContextForm` no longer called when user is null, changing conditional-UI setup on the initial login form, but the comments still describe the old semantics and the responsibility shift is undocumented, risking a regression of conditional UI on the initial login page

adjudication.rationale: In `UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate()`, the WebAuthn conditional UI setup was moved from `if (context.getUser() == null && webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()) { webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context); }` to an unconditional block guarded by `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, where `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` explicitly requires `user != null`. This means that on the initial username+password login screen (where `context.getUser()` is typically null), `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` is no longer called at all (same in the error `challenge(...)` path), which can disable/populate-less conditional passkey UI compared to the previous behavior. That is a concrete behavioral change visible in the diff and can plausibly break conditional UI on first render for flows using `UsernamePasswordForm` directly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: WebAuthn conditional UI re-authentication uses an empty allowList, allowing a different user's passkey to complete re-auth (prompt=login) and potentially swapping identity mid-session

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not show any logic about building or using a WebAuthn allowList during conditional UI or re-authentication. Changes are limited to (a) keeping passkeys UI available when a user is already set (UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null and is used to call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm) and (b) re-authentication form setup via AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError. There is no verifiable evidence in the diff that an empty allowList is used, nor that a different user’s passkey could be accepted and swap identity mid-session.

adjudication_records.issue_text: UsernameForm.authenticate skip condition regression: realm-level passkey policy forces re-auth users without passkeys back to the username form; the UsernameForm path is untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes `UsernameForm.authenticate()` from skipping the username form whenever `context.getUser() != null` to skipping only when `context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` (services/.../UsernameForm.java). That means in realms where conditional passkeys are enabled, re-authentication will no longer bypass the username form, even if the user may not have any passkey credential—potentially an unintended UX/flow change. The added tests exercise re-authentication with passkeys (e.g., `PasskeysUsernameFormTest.webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication`), but there is no test covering the specific edge case of a re-auth user in a passkeys-enabled realm who does *not* have a passkey (to ensure the username form skip behavior is still correct/desired). Whether this is a functional defect can’t be proven from the diff alone because `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` implementation in `UsernameForm` isn’t shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: UsernameForm calls no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() which is not defined in this diff; UsernameForm does not extend UsernamePasswordForm, so code may not compile (or has confusing duplicate logic)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `UsernameForm.authenticate()` now calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` (no-arg), but the diff does not show the full `UsernameForm` file nor its superclass methods. In a unified diff, unchanged methods (including an existing `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` in `UsernameForm` or a parent class) would not appear, so the claim that it is "not defined" and therefore "may not compile" is not verifiable from the diff alone. The added method in `UsernamePasswordForm` has a different signature (`isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel)`), but that does not prove `UsernameForm` lacks its own/no-arg version.

adjudication_records.issue_text: UsernamePasswordForm.challenge/authenticate no longer fills WebAuthn form data on the initial (user==null) login page, potentially breaking initial passkey login rendering for flows built only around UsernamePasswordForm

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the previous behavior where `UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate()` populated WebAuthn/passkeys form context on the initial render when `context.getUser() == null`. Previously it called `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` under `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()` in the user==null branch; now it only calls `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` when `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` is true, and `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` explicitly requires `user != null`. Same change is applied in the error-path `challenge(context, String, String)`. Whether this actually breaks rendering depends on whether another authenticator in the flow now sets up the passkeys UI (not provable from this diff alone), so the “potentially breaking for flows built only around UsernamePasswordForm” part is a compatibility/behavior-change concern rather than a definite defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH visibility changed from protected to public, unnecessarily broadening the SPI API surface

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` in `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator` from `protected static final` to `public static final` (line change shown), which broadens the exposed API surface. This is not a runtime defect, but it is a concrete scope/architecture concern because external code can now reference this constant, increasing SPI/API coupling unnecessarily.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fragile 'assert element absent' test pattern in reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey swallows generic Exceptions, letting unexpected errors like StaleElementReferenceException silently pass; should use assertThrows instead

adjudication.rationale: In `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey()` (added in `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest`), the test checks absence of `//form[@id='webauth']` via a `try { driver.findElement(...); fail(...); } catch (Exception nsee) { // expected }` pattern (appears twice). Because it catches generic `Exception`, unexpected Selenium/runtime failures (e.g., `StaleElementReferenceException`, timing issues, WebDriver errors) would be treated as “expected”, making the test silently pass for the wrong reason. Using `assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` or a dedicated “element not present” helper would be more robust. This is a test-quality issue, not a product defect.
